content: Ofloxacin otic is prescribed to treat infections of the outer ear in both adults and children. It is also used to manage chronic middle ear infections in individuals with a perforated eardrum (a condition where there is a hole in the eardrum) and acute middle ear infections in children with ear tubes. This medication belongs to a class of drugs known as quinolone antibiotics, and it works by eliminating the bacteria responsible for the infection. Ofloxacin otic is available as a liquid solution that is applied directly into the ear. It is typically used once or twice daily for a duration of 7 to 14 days, depending on the condition being treated. It is important to use the medication at the same time(s) each day and to follow the instructions on the prescription label carefully. If you have any questions, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Use the medication exactly as directed and do not use more or less than prescribed. Ofloxacin otic is intended for use in the ears only and should not be used in the eyes. You should start to feel better within the first few days of treatment. If your symptoms do not improve after one week or worsen, contact your doctor. Continue using the medication for the full duration of the prescription, even if you feel better. Stopping the medication too soon or skipping doses may result in incomplete treatment of the infection and could lead to bacterial resistance to antibiotics. To apply the ear drops, follow these steps: 1. Warm the bottle or single-use container in your hand for 1 to 2 minutes to bring the solution to body temperature. 2. Lie down with the affected ear facing upward. 3. Administer the prescribed number of drops or the contents of the prescribed single-use container into the ear. 4. If using a bottle, avoid touching the tip to your ear, fingers, or any other surface to prevent contamination. 5. For middle ear infections, gently press the tragus (the small flap of cartilage near the ear canal) inward four times to help the drops reach the middle ear. 6. Remain lying down with the affected ear facing upward for 5 minutes. 7. Repeat these steps for the opposite ear if necessary. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Before using ofloxacin otic, inform your doctor and pharmacist about all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking or plan to take. Notify your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while using this medication, contact your doctor immediately. Keep the infected ear(s) clean and dry while using ofloxacin otic. Avoid getting the ear(s) wet during bathing and refrain from swimming unless your doctor advises otherwise. Unless instructed otherwise by your doctor, you may continue your normal diet while using this medication. If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not use extra ear drops to make up for a missed dose. Ofloxacin otic may cause side effects. Mild side effects include ear itching or pain, changes in taste, and dizziness. If these symptoms are severe or persistent, inform your doctor. Serious side effects include rash, hives, swelling of the face, throat, tongue, lips, eyes, hands, feet, ankles, or lower legs, hoarseness, and difficulty swallowing or breathing. If you experience any of these symptoms, stop using the medication and contact your doctor immediately. Report any unusual problems while using this medication to your doctor. Store ofloxacin otic in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture, and protect it from light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. In case of accidental ingestion of ofloxacin otic, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor while using this medication. Do not share your medication with others. Your prescription is likely not refillable. If you still have symptoms of infection after completing the course of ofloxacin otic, contact your doctor.
